title: Standard Deduction vs Itemized Deduction: Plain Words Guide
bigPicture: You can lower your tax bill by choosing the bigger deduction between a set amount the government gives you or adding up your own eligible expenses.
whatYouNeedToKnow: The standard deduction is a fixed amount you get automatically without keeping receipts.
Itemized deduction means listing each qualifying expense like medical bills, charity, and mortgage interest.
You pick whichever gives you the larger deduction to pay less tax.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Forgetting to compare both methods and just picking one.
Not keeping records for itemized expenses in case the IRS asks.
actionSteps: Gather your paperwork for things like medical costs, donations, and home loan interest.
Ask a tax helper or use tax software to see which deduction is bigger for you.
